n: God answers the people’s prayer of chapter 14: even if Moses and Samuel—Israel’s greatest intercessors—stood pleading before Me, I wouldn’t change My mind. Send them away. Judgment is now certain.

f.w: Though Moses and Samuel stood before me

n: If they ask where to go, tell them: those destined for death, to death; sword, to sword; famine, to famine; captivity, to captivity. Each will meet the fate their choices led to.

f.w: such as are for the captivity, to the captivity

n: God will send four destroyers: the sword to kill, dogs to drag away, birds and beasts to devour.

f.w: four kinds

n: They will become a horror to all kingdoms because of what King Manasseh did in Jerusalem. Manasseh, Hezekiah’s son, filled the city with idols and innocent blood during his long reign.

f.w: because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah

n: Who will pity you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you or even stop to ask how you are?

f.w: who shall go aside to ask how thou doest?
f.g: Who will turn aside to ask about your peace (shalom)?

n: You rejected Me and kept going backward. So I will stretch out My hand and destroy you; I’m tired of holding back. God had relented many times before.

f.w: I am weary with repenting
f.g: I am tired of relenting (changing My mind about punishment).

n: God will winnow them with a winnowing fork at the city gates, robbing them of children, because they won’t turn from their ways.

f.w: I will fan them with a fan
f.g: Winnow them with a winnowing fork—scatter them like chaff.

n: Widows will be more than the sand of the sea. A destroyer will strike mothers of young men at noon—when no attack is expected.

f.w: a spoiler at noonday
f.g: An attack at midday, a time thought safe.

n: The mother of seven—a picture of complete blessing—faints and breathes her last; her sun sets while it’s still day. Even the most blessed will suffer loss.

f.w: She that hath borne seven
f.g: Seven sons was a sign of perfect fortune (Ruth 4:15; 1 Samuel 2:5).

f.w: her sun is gone down while it was yet day

n: Jeremiah cries: “Woe is me, my mother, that you gave birth to me—a man everyone quarrels with! I’ve neither lent nor borrowed money (which often caused disputes), yet everyone curses me.” His calling has made him an outcast.

f.w: Woe is me, my mother
usury
f.g: Lending at interest; here simply lending and borrowing, which commonly bred conflict.

n: The Lord replies: surely I will strengthen you for good; I will make your enemies plead with you in times of disaster. This came true when Zedekiah later sought Jeremiah’s counsel.

f.w: I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well

n: Can anyone break iron—iron from the north and bronze? A riddle: Babylon’s power from the north can’t be broken by Judah—or, Jeremiah’s God-given strength can’t be broken.

f.w: the northern iron
steel
f.g: Bronze (Hebrew neḥoshet); steel was not yet in common use.

n: God tells Judah: your wealth and treasures will be plundered without payment because of all your sins.

f.w: to the spoil without price

n: You will serve your enemies in a land you don’t know, for God’s anger burns like fire. (Verses 13–14 repeat 17:3-4.)

f.w: a fire is kindled in mine anger

n: Jeremiah prays: Lord, You understand. Remember me and take care of me; avenge me on my persecutors. Don’t let Your patience with them cost me my life. I suffer insults for Your sake.

f.w: for thy sake I have suffered rebuke

n: A beautiful verse: when Your words came, I devoured them, and they became my joy and my heart’s delight, for I bear Your name. Perhaps an echo of the Book of the Law found in Josiah’s day. Scripture can be food for the soul.

f.w: Thy words were found, and I did eat them
I am called by thy name

n: I never sat with the partygoers or joined their fun. Because Your hand was on me, I sat alone, filled with Your indignation at sin. Faithfulness cost him friendships.

f.w: I sat not in the assembly of the mockers
I sat alone because of thy hand

n: Why is my pain endless and my wound incurable? Will You be to me like a deceptive brook that dries up when needed? An astonishingly honest prayer from a weary prophet.

f.w: as waters that fail
f.g: A wadi or stream that dries up in summer—disappointing the thirsty.

n: God responds with a gentle rebuke: if you turn back to Me, I will restore you and you’ll stand before Me. If you speak what is precious, not what is worthless, you’ll be My mouthpiece. Let them turn to you—don’t turn to them.

f.w: If thou return
f.g: Even the prophet is called to “return” (repent) from discouragement.

f.w: thou shalt be as my mouth
take forth the precious from the vile
f.g: Separate what is valuable from what is worthless, like refining metal.

n: God renews the promise from Jeremiah’s call: I will make you a fortified bronze wall. They will fight you but won’t win, for I am with you to save and rescue you.

f.w: a fenced brasen wall
I am with thee to save thee

n: I will rescue you from the hands of the wicked and redeem you from the grip of the ruthless.

f.w: I will redeem thee
the terrible
